your_private_thoughts_last_10.thought: No building legal; preserve $167 and $175 mortgage capacity. Next build Boardwalk's third house. Avoid facilitating rival monopolies; dark blues remain the only developed set.
Save the $50 for dark-blue development. Jail preserves cash while opponents can still pay our rents; no urgent acquisition warrants paying to leave.

Deny Claude the final pink and gain valuable trade leverage. $7 cash remains, but Reading/Water Works supply $175 mortgage capacity and Virginia another $80. No developed rival sets, so liquidity risk is manageable; avoid trading Virginia cheaply into a monopoly.

Virginia blocks Claude's pink monopoly. Keep it; no need to mortgage until cash is required. $7 cash plus $255 mortgage capacity is adequate against undeveloped rivals. Building unavailable; prioritize third houses on dark blues when legal, ideally funded by rent.

$230 undervalues a monopoly blocker. $550 funds third houses on both dark blues plus reserves while exhausting Claude's cash, limiting immediate pink development. No need to sell cheaply: undeveloped opposing properties pose little liquidity risk.

$300 leaves Claude ample cash to develop pinks while funding only one blue house. $500 funds both third houses and reserves while reducing his immediate building capacity. No urgency: Reading and Water Works provide $175 mortgage liquidity against undeveloped rivals.

$450 leaves $482, enough for both third houses plus $82 reserve, while Claude retains only $103 before mortgages. $375 gives too little cushion for enabling pinks. No urgent liquidity risk against undeveloped rivals; happy to retain the blocker if declined.

Claude has repeatedly raised his bid, so hold at $450. Selling enables pinks and his substantial mortgage capacity; require the extra reserve. No imminent liquidity crisis warrants conceding, with $175 available from Reading and Water Works.

The offered $250 plus light blues yields only $360 after mortgages, short of both third houses. $350 plus both yields $460 liquidity, improves future leverage, and removes $110 of Claude's mortgage capacity. Prefer this to $450 cash; otherwise retain the pink blocker.

$325 plus both deeds provides $467 after their mortgages, funding both third houses with $67 reserve while preserving Reading/Water Works liquidity. Removes Claude's light-blue mortgage assets and retains future bargaining leverage. Worth conceding $25 to close.
